site.name: aurora-network
site.summary: Aurora Network — Privacy & Audience (local demo) Fictional social network. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly in a browser. Pages `index.html` — Privacy overview Entry hub. Four cards (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) link to each privacy-management surface. Below the cards, a "Snapshot" panel summarizes the user's current privacy state as a key/value list. `audience.html` — Default audience Radio-group selector with four options (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me). Below the selector: dynamic explanation of who can see new posts, custom-list manager (create / inspect / view recent use), and a "Who can tag you?" radio block. `tag-review.html` — Pending tag queue

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full aurora-network system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Aurora Network privacy settings demonstrate strong clarity in audience selection with immediate, descriptive feedback. However, the Tag Review workflow suffers from critical inconsistencies: 'Hide all' executes destructively without confirmation (unlike 'Approve all'), and individual actions lack visual state updates, leaving users uncertain if their moderation choices registered. Additionally, mobile usability is compromised by navigation and action buttons falling below the 44px touch target guideline.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the Aurora Network privacy settings, focusing on the flow from the overview dashboard to specific configuration pages (Audience, Tags, History, Muted Words), validating state changes, feedback loops, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will begin at the Privacy Overview hub, verifying the 'Snapshot' panel accuracy. It will then systematically traverse the four primary privacy modules: configuring Default Audience (including custom lists), processing the Tag Review queue, testing Past Post Visibility filters, and managing Muted Words. Each phase includes validation of UI feedback and error states, concluding with a mobile viewport check for touch target accessibility given the prescan warnings.
assumptions: The 'Change' links in the Snapshot panel on index.html route directly to the relevant sub-pages or open modals.
Actions taken on sub-pages (e.g., changing audience) may require a page reload or navigation back to index.html to reflect in the Snapshot summary.
The 'Custom list' manager on audience.html allows for creation/inspection without leaving the page context.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (<44px) identified in prescan across all pages (mobile risk).
Past post visibility bulk actions (potential for irreversible data loss if UX is unclear).
Tag review queue management (efficiency of bulk approve/hide vs individual actions).
State synchronization between sub-pages and the Index.html Snapshot panel.

Check 'Snapshot' panel values match expected defaults (e.g., Audience: Friends).

phases.title: Default Audience Configuration

key_checks: Toggle through all 4 radio options (Public, Friends, Custom, Only Me).
Verify dynamic explanation text updates correctly for each option.

phases.title: Tag Review Workflow
phases.objective: Evaluate the efficiency of the moderation queue for pending tags.
key_checks: Review the 7 pending items for content clarity (who tagged, context).
Test individual actions: Approve, Hide tag, Block user.

Verify if 'Block user' triggers a confirmation dialog or immediate action.

phases.title: Historical Data & Bulk Actions

key_checks: Test year filter dropdowns (2019-2026).

phases.title: Muted Words Management

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical flows on mobile viewport, specifically targeting the prescan's 'small tap target' warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/Pixel 5).
Attempt to tap 'Change' links in Snapshot panel (verify precision required).

Specific usability issues documented for reporting.

notes: Prescan indicates no JS errors, but layout warnings suggest significant mobile usability risks due to <44px tap targets.
The 'Snapshot' on index.html is a key feedback loop; always return there after making changes to verify persistence.
Past post visibility involves 'irreversible' bulk actions; look closely for undo mechanisms or strong warnings.

findings.problem: Inconsistent safety mechanisms for bulk actions; 'Hide all' executes immediately without confirmation, while 'Approve all' triggers a modal.
findings.evidence: Steps-79-80 show 'Hide all' clicked with no modal appearing and no visible text change, whereas steps-55-60 confirm 'Approve all' triggers a 'Approve all 7 pending tags?' confirmation dialog. This asymmetry creates a high risk of accidental data loss or unintended content hiding.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect consistent friction for destructive or bulk operations. The lack of a 'point of no return' check for 'Hide all' violates standard UX patterns for mass-editing tools, leading to potential trust erosion if users accidentally hide legitimate tags.
findings.suggestion: Implement a confirmation modal for 'Hide all' identical in structure to the 'Approve all' modal, clearly stating the consequence (tags will not link to profile) and offering Cancel/Confirm options.

findings.problem: Lack of immediate visual feedback after clicking 'Approve', 'Hide tag', or 'Block user' on individual items.
findings.evidence: Steps-37-42 and 73-78 note that after clicking 'Approve' or 'Hide tag', the counter remains at '7 tags waiting for review' and the item remains visible in the list. No strikethrough, dimming, or removal animation occurs.
findings.why_it_matters: Without optimistic UI updates or immediate state changes, users are left guessing whether the system registered their click. This forces them to manually refresh or wait for a slow server response, creating anxiety and perceived sluggishness.
findings.suggestion: Implement optimistic UI: immediately remove the card from the list or visually disable it (e.g., grey out, add checkmark icon) upon click, and decrement the counter instantly.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact on mobile devices
findings.problem: Critical navigation and action tap targets are below the recommended 44px minimum height for touch interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps-19-24 and final_observation identify sidebar links (37px height), the Aurora logo (28px height), and individual action buttons like 'Approve' (41px height) as failing mobile accessibility guidelines.
findings.why_it_matters: Sub-44px targets increase error rates for touch users, leading to frustration and accidental clicks on adjacent elements. This is particularly problematic for frequent actions like 'Approve' in a moderation queue.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding on sidebar links and action buttons to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px, even if the visual icon/text is smaller.

findings.problem: Ambiguous save behavior for 'Who can tag you?' settings compared to 'Default audience'.
findings.evidence: Steps-25-30 observe that changing 'Default audience' requires a 'Save default' button which provides a success banner. However, changing 'Who can tag you?' radio buttons updates the visual state immediately but offers no save button or confirmation toast.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent interaction models within the same page confuse users about which settings are auto-saved and which require explicit commitment. Users may unnecessarily look for a save button for tagging preferences or assume they haven't been saved.
findings.suggestion: Either add a 'Save' button for the tagging section to match the audience section, or explicitly label the tagging section as 'Auto-saved' with a subtle checkmark animation upon change.
